transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Any time I have to get blood drawn, I go to great lengths to avoid it or sit there in sheer terror the whole time. It has gotten to the point where it is really interfering with my healthcare, so my son insisted I come speak with someone about it.
Can you tell me if your fear is specifically related to the sight of blood, the pain of the needle, or something else about the blood draw process?

It is really the thought of the needle going into my vein, which just feels incredibly dangerous to me now. I have this terrible dread that I will faint and pass out again, just like when I fell and broke my wrist. Even seeing a picture of a blood draw on a clinic poster makes my heart pound and makes me feel light-headed.
Have you been avoiding other medical procedures or situations besides blood draws due to similar fears or anxieties, or is your avoidance mainly focused on blood draws and injections?

My fear is really just focused on the blood draws and needles, rather than other medical procedures. For instance, I did cancel my cataract surgery, but that was solely because they required pre-operative blood tests first that I just couldn't bring myself to do. Other than that, I have no issues with my usual doctor visits.

Can you describe how you feel when you're not thinking about or confronted with blood draws or needles - do you generally feel anxious or worried about your health, or is it really just this specific situation that causes you distress?

I don't worry about my health in general at all, and I actually want to take care of myself, like getting that cataract surgery done. It is strictly the specific situation of having a needle put into my vein that triggers this intense terror. Otherwise, I feel completely fine and normal.
Can you tell me if your fear of needles or blood draws has been present for as long as you can remember, or if it started after a specific event, like the time you fell and broke your wrist?

No, I never had this fear before; it started entirely after that incident about a year ago. Before I fainted and broke my wrist during that routine blood test, I never had any trouble with needles or lab work. It was only after that fall that this terrible terror began.

Can you tell me if you have been experiencing any other bodily symptoms or concerns about your health besides this specific fear of needles and blood draws, such as excessive worry about having a serious illness?
No, I don't have any worries like that at all. I don't stress about having a serious illness, and my main issue is really just the intense fear and avoidance related to the blood draws themselves.

You mentioned your fear is specifically about the needle going into your vein and the associated danger, but can you tell me if you also fear other aspects of medical procedures, such as the results of the blood test or the potential consequences of not having the blood drawn?

No, my fear isn't about the test results or the consequences of missing the tests at all. It is strictly about the physical act of the needle going into my vein, the fear of fainting, and the dread of getting hurt again like I did during that fall.
Does the fear of fainting or the fear of the needle itself cause more distress for you when you're faced with a blood draw?

Honestly, both are deeply intertwined and absolutely terrifying to me. The thought of the needle going into my vein feels incredibly dangerous, but the fear of fainting again is just as massive because of my previous fall and wrist fracture. Just the thought of passing out like that again makes me feel light-headed and completely panicked.
Can you think of any situations or stimuli other than blood draws or needles that trigger a similar intense fear or anxiety response in you?

No, there is absolutely nothing else that triggers this kind of fear in me. It is strictly limited to needles, blood draws, or even seeing a picture of a blood draw on a clinic poster. No other situations or objects in my life cause this kind of anxiety at all.
When you experience the fear of fainting or the needle going into your vein, do you also worry that you might die or have a severe medical emergency as a result?

I don't worry that I am actually going to die, though I do get a strong, vague sense that something terrible is bound to happen because the situation feels so dangerous. My primary fear is simply passing out again and hurting myself, just like when I fell and broke my wrist.
Can you describe any specific physical sensations or symptoms you experience when you're confronted with the thought or sight of a blood draw, such as a racing heart, sweating, or trembling?

Yes, if I even see a picture of a blood draw, my heart starts pounding, my hands get clammy, and I feel a swooping light-headedness as if I might pass out right there. When I actually have to go through with it, I sit in the chair shaking and gripping the armrests with my eyes squeezed shut. It is a very intense physical reaction every single time.

Have you ever experienced a similar intense fear or anxiety response to other specific objects or situations, such as heights, enclosed spaces, or certain animals, besides the fear of needles and blood draws?
No, I have never experienced this kind of intense fear with anything else, like heights or animals. This terror is entirely specific to needles and having my blood drawn ever since my fall last year.

Can you tell me if your fear of needles and blood draws is primarily driven by a fear of the physical act itself or if you also worry about the potential health implications or consequences of having a blood test, even though you mentioned earlier that you don't worry about having a serious illness?

It is entirely driven by the physical act itself and the immediate physical consequences, rather than any health implications of the test. Just knowing a needle is going into my vein feels terribly dangerous, and my main worry is fainting, losing control, or falling and hurting myself again like before. I don't worry at all about what the medical results might show.

Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to your fear of needles and blood draws, beyond just avoiding medical procedures that involve them?

Yes, it has absolutely disrupted my social life and daily routines. Besides avoiding medical care, I've had to rearrange or miss my walking club sessions and my volunteer work at the senior center because I am so consumed by avoiding or worrying about these blood draws.

Can you tell me if you experience any excessive or persistent fear, anxiety, or avoidance of other situations or objects beyond blood draws and needles that might be causing you significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

No, I don't have this kind of reaction to any other objects or situations in my life. This intense fear and avoidance are strictly limited to blood draws and needles, all stemming from that one incident where I fainted and broke my wrist. Otherwise, I go about my daily life without any other fears or anxieties like this.
Is your fear of needles and blood draws exclusively triggered by the sight or thought of the needle entering your vein, or are there other aspects of the procedure that also contribute to your fear?

While the needle entering my vein is a major trigger, the fear is also deeply tied to the dread of fainting and getting light-headed again, just like when I fell and broke my wrist. In fact, even just seeing a picture of a blood draw on a clinic poster is enough to trigger a pounding heart, clammy hands, and that awful dizzy feeling.

You've mentioned that your fear is very specific to the needle going into your vein and the associated fear of fainting, but can you tell me if you've experienced any other panic attacks or intense anxiety episodes outside of situations involving blood draws or needles?
No, I have never had a panic attack or felt that kind of intense anxiety in any other situation. Outside of blood draws and needles, I feel completely normal and at ease.
Do you experience any fear or anxiety related to other bodily sensations, such as pain or discomfort, outside of the context of blood draws and needles?

No, not at all. My fear and anxiety are strictly limited to blood draws, needles, and the thought of fainting during those specific procedures. I don't experience any fear or anxiety about other bodily sensations, pain, or general discomfort outside of that context.

Can you tell me if you have experienced any other intense fears or anxiety episodes in response to other specific objects, situations, or activities that are not related to blood draws or needles, which might help us understand if your fear is part of a broader pattern of anxiety?

No, I haven't experienced any other intense fears or anxiety like this with other things. This fear is strictly limited to blood draws and needles. I don't have any broader pattern of anxiety or other phobias at all.
Have you ever considered that your fear might be related to a deeper concern about losing control or a general anxiety about medical procedures, rather than just the needle itself?

I haven't really thought about it as a loss of control, and I don't think it's a general fear of medical procedures, considering I was actually looking forward to my cataract surgery and only canceled it because of the required blood draw. My fear is very specifically about the needle going into my vein and the terrifying prospect of fainting and hurting myself again.
Is there anything else that you fear could happen to you during a blood draw, besides fainting and the needle going into your vein, that contributes to your overall anxiety about the procedure?

I can't really think of anything else specific. It really just comes down to the needle itself, the fear of passing out again like last time, and that vague, overwhelming feeling that something terrible is bound to happen.

Can you tell me if you have ever worried that you might have an underlying illness or condition that could be worsened by the blood draw or needle, or if your fear is purely focused on the act of the needle going into your vein and the immediate physical consequences?

No, I don't worry about an underlying illness being worsened at all. My fear is entirely focused on the physical act of the needle going into my vein and the terrifying sensation of feeling light-headed and fainting again, just like when I fell and broke my wrist.

Have you ever experienced any similar episodes of intense fear or anxiety in response to other specific objects or situations that are not related to blood draws or needles, even if they are not as severe?
No, I really haven't experienced this kind of intense fear with anything else in my life. It seems to be just this one specific issue with blood draws and needles that triggers me.

Have you ever experienced a similar intense fear or anxiety response to other specific situations or objects that are not related to blood draws or needles, which might suggest a broader anxiety issue rather than a specific phobia?

No, I haven't experienced this kind of intense fear with anything else at all. This extreme anxiety is strictly limited to needles and having my blood drawn. There are no other situations or objects in my life that bother me like this.

You've mentioned that your fear is very specific to blood draws and needles, but can you tell me if there's anything else in your life that you avoid or find extremely distressing, even if it's not as severe as your reaction to blood draws?

No, there is absolutely nothing else in my life that I avoid or find distressing. My anxiety and avoidance are entirely focused on blood draws, needles, and the fear of fainting again. Before that fall last year, everything else in my life was completely fine.

You've described your fear as being very specific to blood draws and needles, but I want to clarify: do you think your fear would generalize to other medical procedures that involve similar sensations, such as injections or IVs, or is it exclusively about the blood draw itself?

Yes, it would definitely apply to IVs as well, because my fear is highly focused on a needle entering my vein, which is what led to me fainting before. A standard injection, like a flu shot in the arm muscle, doesn't terrify me the same way. It is specifically the thought of anything going into my veins that makes me panic.

You mentioned your fear would apply to IVs, but how do you feel about other medical procedures that might involve some level of pain or discomfort, such as dental work or minor surgeries, and do you avoid those as well?

I don't have any fear of dental work or other medical procedures just because of pain or discomfort. The only reason I canceled my cataract surgery was because it required those pre-operative blood draws that I couldn't face. As long as a procedure doesn't involve needles in my veins or blood tests, I don't have any issue with it at all.

Can you think of any situation where you would be willing to undergo a blood draw or a similar procedure, such as if it were absolutely necessary for a life-threatening condition, or do you think your fear would prevent you from doing so under any circumstances?

I don't think it would completely stop me in a life-or-death emergency, even though it was powerful enough to make me cancel my cataract surgery. When I absolutely cannot avoid a blood draw, I can only get through it if my son or a neighbor comes with me. Even then, I have to endure it in sheer terror, gripping the armrests with my eyes squeezed shut.

Have you ever experienced a panic attack or felt an overwhelming sense of fear in situations unrelated to blood draws, needles, or medical procedures, which might help us understand the scope of your anxiety?

No, I have never experienced that kind of overwhelming fear or panic in any other situation. My anxiety is strictly limited to blood draws and procedures that involve needles in my veins. Outside of those specific medical situations, I feel completely fine.

Can you tell me if you have ever experienced any other intense fears or anxiety episodes that are not related to blood draws or needles, but might be triggered by other specific objects, situations, or activities?

No, I have never experienced any other intense fears or anxiety episodes related to other objects or situations. This severe fear of blood draws and needles is the only issue of this kind that I have, and it only started after my fall last year.
